original_interpretation: SIA/BCG: ~USD 110bn industry capex globally in 2019.
evidence_found: "Overall, we estimate that in 2019 the industry invested about $90 billion in R&D and $110 billion in capital expenditure globally across all the activities in the value chain." (p. 22)
notes: Historical 2019 estimate, labelled as such.

original_interpretation: SIA/BCG 2021: state-of-the-art fab needs ~USD 5bn (advanced analog) to USD 20bn (advanced logic/memory) capex.
evidence_found: "A state-of-the-art semiconductor fab of standard capacity requires roughly $5 billion (for advanced analog fabs) to $20 billion (for advanced logic and memory fabs) of capital expenditure, including land, building, and equipment." (p. 18)
correction: Accurate for the 2021 report, but the top end is dated: Tom's Hardware (16 Jul 2026) puts a leading-edge 2nm-class fab module (~20k wafer starts/month) at roughly USD 25-35bn to build and equip (new claim @c_2nm_fab). Present USD 5-20bn as a circa-2020 range.
notes: Range includes land, building and equipment (not stated in claim).

original_interpretation: SIA/BCG 2021: a single EUV machine can cost ~USD 150m.
evidence_found: "A single EUV machine can cost $150 million." (p. 20)
correction: Superseded: CNBC (22 May 2025) says EUV machines sold in 2024 started at USD 220m and High NA costs more than USD 400m (new claims @c_euv_220, @c_highna_400); Reuters ~USD 250m (CLM-1751).

original_interpretation: IDMs are vertically integrated, doing design, fabrication and ATP in-house.
evidence_found: SIA/BCG: "IDMs are vertically integrated across multiple parts of the value chain, performing design; fabrication; and assembly, packaging and test activities in- house." (p. 24). White House: "The earliest semiconductor firms performed all three steps in-house and today are known as integrated device manufacturers (IDMs)." (p. 26)
notes: SIA/BCG adds that some IDMs run hybrid 'fab-lite' models.

original_interpretation: SIA/BCG: IDMs ~70% of global semiconductor sales in 2019.
evidence_found: "IDMs accounted for approximately 70% of the global semiconductor sales in 2019." (p. 24)
notes: Historical 2019 estimate.

original_interpretation: Fabless firms focus on design and outsource fabrication and ATP.
evidence_found: SIA/BCG: "Fabless firms choose to focus on design and outsource fabrication as well as assembly, packaging, and testing." (p. 24). CSET: "a fabless firm designs and sells the chip and purchases fabrication services from a foundry and ATP services from an outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (OSAT) firm" (p. 6)
notes: CSET quote in the claim's evidence is slightly altered ('purchase') and located on p. 6, not p. 5.

original_interpretation: Foundries make chips for third parties, serving fabless firms and IDMs lacking capacity.
evidence_found: SIA/BCG: "Foundries address the fabrication needs of fabless firms and IDMs alike, as most IDMs do not have sufficient installed manufacturing capacity in-house to cover all their needs." (p. 25). CSET: "foundries, i.e., fabs operating independently and manufacturing chips for third-party customers" (p. 19)

original_interpretation: SIA/BCG 2021: foundries ~35% of total manufacturing capacity.
evidence_found: "Currently foundries account for 35% of the total industry manufacturing capacity, or 50% if memory is excluded. Their share rises to 78% in advanced (14 nanometers or below)..." (p. 25)
notes: 'Currently' = circa 2019-2020 (exhibit labelled Capacity (2019)); dated figure.

original_interpretation: OSATs provide ATP under contract to IDMs and fabless firms.
evidence_found: "OSATs provide assembly, packaging and test services under contract to both IDMs and fabless companies." (p. 25)

original_interpretation: Semiconductor-grade polysilicon ~1,000x purer than solar grade; top-4 suppliers >90% share.
evidence_found: "the polysilicon employed to make the silicon ingot ... is required to have a purity level that is 1,000 times higher than the level required for solar energy panels, and is provided primarily by just four companies, with a combined global market share above 90%." (p. 21)
notes: Circa 2019-2020 estimate; no company names given.

original_interpretation: Mainland China + Taiwan >60% of world ATP capacity.
evidence_found: "In terms of capacity location, mainland China and Taiwan account for more than 60% of the world's assembly, packaging and testing capacity." (p. 35)
notes: Circa 2020 figure.

original_interpretation: 9 of 10 largest OSATs by revenue HQ in mainland China, Taiwan, Singapore.
evidence_found: "Today 9 of the 10 largest OSAT firms by revenue are headquartered in mainland China, Taiwan and Singapore." (p. 35)
notes: As of 2021 report; ranking may have changed since. claim_type estimate is acceptable (BCG analysis).

original_interpretation: BCG 2024 projects US share of <10nm logic capacity from nearly zero (2022) to 28% (2032).
evidence_found: BCG: "for the most advanced logic chips—those newer than 10 nanometers—... with the US increasing its share from nearly zero in 2022 to 28% in 2032." SIA summary: "U.S. capacity for advanced logic will grow from 0% in 2022 to 28% by 2032" (p. 1)
notes: May 2024 projection based on announced investments; not an outcome.

original_interpretation: BCG 2024 projects USD 2.3tn wafer-fab investment 2024-2032 vs USD 720bn prior decade.
evidence_found: "We project $2.3 trillion in new investment in wafer fabrication between 2024–2032, compared with $720 billion in the 10 years prior." (BCG web article)
notes: SIA summary frames the same USD 2.3tn as 'global capital expenditures in the semiconductor industry in the coming decade'.

original_interpretation: BCG expects ATP to diversify to SE Asia, LatAm, E. Europe; materials stay concentrated in East Asia.
evidence_found: "in assembly, test, and packaging (ATP), we expect the capacity footprint to diversify from Mainland China and Taiwan to Southeast Asia, Latin America, and Eastern Europe"; "although materials production will remain concentrated in East Asia, we expect it to follow future fab capacity to the United States and Europe"

original_interpretation: CSET 2022: at least 81% of world ATP capacity in Asia; North America ~3% of packaging capacity.
evidence_found: "the Semiconductor Industry Association estimates that at least 81 percent of the world's ATP capacity is physically located in Asia." (p. 16); "North America's share of global packaging capacity is only 3 percent." (p. 16)
correction: The 81% figure is an SIA estimate quoted by CSET, not CSET's own facility analysis; attribute as 'SIA estimate cited by CSET (2022)'. The metric methodology 'CSET analysis of facility data' is wrong.

original_interpretation: Advanced packaging provided in-house by IDMs/foundries or by OSATs for third parties.
evidence_found: "Advanced packaging, like conventional packaging, is currently provided via two business models: (1) in-house ATP services performed by IDMs and foundries post- fabrication; and (2) OSAT firms for third-party customers." (p. 11)

original_interpretation: CSET 2022: Japan+Korea+Taiwan ~69% of IC substrate capacity; ABF substrates in acute shortage.
evidence_found: "There are 26 IC substrate production facilities spread between Japan (14), South Korea (7), and Taiwan (5), collectively representing 69 percent of global capacity." (p. 32); "there is an especially acute shortage of the IC substrate material. Of particular concern are Ajinomoto Build Up film substrates." (p. 21)
notes: Shortage describes 2021-22 conditions; do not present as current.

original_interpretation: 2021 US 100-day review split the chain into five segments.
evidence_found: "This report examines the semiconductor supply chain through five related essential segments: (1) design; (2) fabrication; (3) assembly, test, and packaging (ATP) and advanced packaging; (4) materials; and (5) manufacturing equipment." (p. 22; repeated p. 27)

original_interpretation: In fabless/foundry model each step done by a different specialised company.
evidence_found: "In the fabless/foundry model, each of these three steps is performed by a different company that specializes in its role in the supply chain." (p. 27)

original_interpretation: US share of global semiconductor production fell from 37% (1990) to 12% by 2021.
evidence_found: "The U.S. share of global semiconductor production has dropped from 37 percent in 1990 to 12 percent today" (p. 9); p. 37: "[U.S.] capacity accounts for approximately 12 percent of the global total, down from 37 percent in 1990." Newer, SIA summary: "decreasing from 37% in 1990 to 12% in 2020, and further declining to 10% as of 2022."
correction: Measure is fab capacity, not production, and the 12% is for 2020 (not 2021). Newer: 10% as of 2022 (SIA/BCG 2024; new claim @c_us_cap, also CLM-0563).
notes: Locator is p. 9, not p. 8.

original_interpretation: SEMI describes silicon wafers as the fundamental building material for most semiconductors.
evidence_found: "Silicon wafers are the fundamental building material for the majority of semiconductors, which are vital components of all electronic devices."
notes: Industry-body description; claim correctly framed as 'SEMI describes'.

original_interpretation: 2025 wafer shipments 12,973 MSI (+5.8%); revenue -1.2% to USD 11.4bn.
evidence_found: "Worldwide silicon wafer shipments in 2025 increased 5.8% to 12,973 million square inches (MSI) while wafer revenue slipped 1.2% to $11.4 billion over the same period, the SEMI Silicon Manufacturers Group (SMG) reported" (press release, 10 Feb 2026)
notes: Latest annual figure (2026 data due early 2027). Browser hit a Cloudflare check; web_extract returned the text.

original_interpretation: WSTS Spring 2026: 2026 market USD 1.51tn (+90%), memory ~+250%.
evidence_found: "the global semiconductor market is now projected to grow 90 percent in 2026, reaching USD 1.51 trillion."; Memory "is forecast to surge by around 250 percent year over year, reaching more than USD 800 billion in 2026."
notes: Forecast, correctly labelled. 'Recent News Release' URL is overwritten by each new release; still the Spring 2026 release on 2026-10-01. Also gives 2027 forecast ~USD 1.9tn (+27%).

original_interpretation: ASML is the only manufacturer of EUV lithography systems.
evidence_found: ASML: "ASML is currently the world's only manufacturer of EUV lithography systems." (Annual Report 2025, p. 17). CSET: "One Dutch firm, ASML, exclusively produces EUV scanners, the most advanced photolithography equipment." (p. 32)
notes: CSET locator is p. 32, not p. 30. Company self-statement corroborated by independent CSET; fact type acceptable.

original_interpretation: ASML reports ~5,100 suppliers.
evidence_found: "5,100 Total number of suppliers" (At a glance, p. 5); "5,100 Total number of suppliers 2024: 5,150" (p. 42)

original_interpretation: ASML 2025: IBM EUR 8.2bn vs EUR 24.6bn new system sales (EUV 11.6, DUV 12.0).
evidence_found: "EUV system sales increased 39% to €11.6 billion"; "DUV system sales decreased 6% to €12.0 billion"; "Installed Base Management sales increased 26% to €8.2 billion" (p. 7); "2025 Net system sales €24,474 million" (p. 9)
correction: Net system sales were EUR 24,474m (~EUR 24.5bn), not EUR 24.6bn; they include EUR 825m metrology & inspection besides EUV and DUV. See new claim @c_asml_sys25.
notes: IBM = 'net service and field option sales'.

original_interpretation: ASML recognized revenue on 48 EUV systems in 2025.
evidence_found: "EUV system sales increased 39% to €11.6 billion, recognized revenue on 48 EUV systems (NXE & EXE)" (p. 7)

original_interpretation: TSMC says it adheres to the pure-play foundry model.
evidence_found: "Our success is predicated on our steadfast adherence to the pure-play foundry business model." (Letter to Shareholders, p. 011)

original_interpretation: TSMC 2025: 12,682 products for 534 customers.
evidence_found: "We deployed 305 distinct process technologies, and manufactured 12,682 products for 534 customers." (Highlights of 2025, Letter to Shareholders)
notes: Highlights sit on the pp. 010-011 spread, not p. 009.

original_interpretation: 7nm and below = 74% of TSMC 2025 wafer revenue.
evidence_found: "Advanced technologies (7-nanometer and beyond) accounted for 74 percent of total wafer revenue, up from 69 percent in 2024."
notes: 3nm alone was 24% of 2025 wafer revenue.

original_interpretation: TrendForce: TSMC 72.5% of combined top-10 foundry revenue in 2Q26; Samsung 5.9%, SMIC 5.4%.
evidence_found: "TSMC maintained its lead with 2Q26 revenue nearing $40.2 billion ... capturing a 72.5% market share."; Samsung "market share declined to 5.9%"; SMIC "market share edged up to 5.4%"; "combined revenue of the world's top 10 foundries rose 11.5% QoQ to nearly US$53.49 billion"
correction: Percentages verified, but they are not shares of top-10 combined revenue: TSMC's US$40.2bn is 75.2% of US$53.49bn. The 72.5%/5.9% shares imply a denominator of ~US$55bn (wider foundry total). See new claim @c_tf_tsmc.

original_interpretation: TrendForce: Samsung 39.4% of DRAM revenue 2Q26.
evidence_found: "this lifted Samsung's quarterly revenue to $60.98 billion, up 63.4% QoQ. The company ranked first with a market share of 39.4%."; industry revenue "nearly US$154.73 billion in 2Q26"

original_interpretation: TrendForce: SK hynix 24.9% of DRAM revenue 2Q26.
evidence_found: "SK hynix ranked second. ... Its 2Q26 revenue increased 37.9% QoQ to $38.59 billion, while market share edged down to 24.9%."
